traits.notes: The seedling exhibits a distinct whorled leaf arrangement with a glossy, rugose leaf surface. There are visible holes and tears on several leaf margins. A pink and white tag is partially visible near the base of the stem.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves, approximately 6-7, are clearly seen radiating from a single central node on the stem)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped in a rosette-like arrangement at the apex of the seedling)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf blade is undivided and attached directly to the petiole)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (margins are smooth, though some leaves show irregular holes due to damage)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are widest near the base and taper gradually to the tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the tip extends into a long, slender point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the base of the leaf tapers down the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a distinct midrib is visible with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): highly visible and prominent (veins are deeply impressed on the upper surface, creating a rugose texture; numerous parallel secondary veins branch from the midrib)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny and rugose (the leaf surface is glossy and has a bumpy texture due to the sunken veins)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are very brief, making the leaves appear to emerge directly from the stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical and smooth)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stem appears thick, rigid, and lignified)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem surface appears smooth and hairless)
    19. Stem color: dark brown to reddish-brown (visible at the base of the leaves)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears relatively uniform without obvious ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf axils)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no distinct swollen joint is visible at the base of the petiole)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent

F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a distinct whorled leaf arrangement with a glossy, rugose leaf surface. There are visible holes and tears on several leaf margins. A pink and white tag is partially visible near the base of the stem.
